findings.claim: Five of the seven methods, including 'CLDs in their participatory variant', are 'fundamentally participatory practices'
findings.failure_mode: Overstated for CLDs: the source says CLDs put 'a lot of power in the researcher's hands' and are 'created with a lot of control by researchers'; Fig 1.2 singles out PSM and FCM as participation-emphasising
findings.fix: correct: Rich Pictures, Theory of Change, PSM and FCM are routinely participatory; CLDs, BBNs and System Dynamics can be run participatively

findings.claim: Ch 10 advice is concrete, e.g. "30- to 60-minute chunks", "transcription takes 5–6× the recording length", "the trick is in having the confidence to move between steps openly and with purpose, but to do so in a systematic way" [V]
findings.failure_mode: First two quoted fragments are not verbatim (source: 'thirty- or sixty-minute chunks'; 'Transcription can easily take five or six times the length of the recording'); the [V] third quote is from Ch 8 (System Dynamics, iterating between modelling steps), not the Ch 10 workshop runbook
findings.fix: correct: quote verbatim ('thirty- or sixty-minute chunks'; 'can easily take five or six times the length of the recording') and drop the Ch 8 quote or cite it to Ch 8

findings.claim: 'A boundary object is a thing different stakeholders can engage with from their own perspectives without losing their identity — it absorbs different interpretations without collapsing into any one.'
findings.failure_mode: Definition of Star & Griesemer's concept supplied from outside the source; the book gives no definition (it says maps help build consensus, find where disagreements are, and 'preserve ideas and represent both sides')
findings.fix: correct: The map is a shared object people learn around; it can help build consensus, locate disagreements, and represent both sides where they are not resolved (Ch 9)

notes: This distillation quotes the source far more than the deep ref does: about 25 [V] quotations were re-extracted from the converted text at Pass G (a projection-protocol breach). All were checked by normalised text match and every [V] quotation is verbatim in its cited section. Grading rule: where the deep ref holds the core claim and the quote adds source-verified wording or detail, graded FAITHFUL (Concepts 2, 3, 6, 8-10, 12, 14-18, 20, 21, 25, 26); where the core claim is absent from the deep ref, graded UNSUPPORTED as a DEEP-REF GAP (D004, D005, D010, D011, D015). Fix these by extending the deep ref, not by stripping. Also: line 18's 'fixator-burnout' is a garble of 'facilitator burnout' (Ch 10). Integration rows for Liberating Structures, NHS Just Culture and OpenStax OB (bases of power, resource dependence, in-group/out-group, groupthink) check out. The worked example is hypothetical and does not present outcomes as the source's findings. Most serious: D025/D024 (fabricated Ostrom borrowed-through and integration row), D019 (false provenance claim that the re-extracted passages are in the deep ref), D023 (non-corpus Mitchell-Agle-Wood row).
